plantfinder.mobot.org (Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder) refused this machine (fetch status: error:ConnectError) -- could not be read; not used for any field, and nothing from it was guessed.

attracts_pollinators is TRUE based on an unconditional statement ('...emits a strong odor of rotten flesh to attract pollinators') and NC State's structured Attracts: field also lists 'Pollinators'. Note the same page separately says the smell attracts 'carrion flies and midges, which pollinate the flowers' -- carrion flies/midges are not among the named pollinator taxa in the task's rule, but the unconditional 'attract pollinators' sentence and the structured Attracts:Pollinators field independently support TRUE.
Species is not a vine/climber (NC State Habit/Form: 'Erect'), so the climber size-nulling rule does not apply.

No page found addressing whether the plant is a named-cultivar-only size record -- the RHS and NC State figures used are for the species Amorphophallus konjac itself, not a cultivar (a cultivar 'Black Sox' is mentioned on NC State only for stem/spadix color, not size).

Also on the pages (noted at landing, verified against the cached copies): NC State's Edibility field in full reads 'The tubers are starchy and edible when cooked like a potato. It is commonly dried and ground into a flour and used in noodles and tofu. Can be toxic if eaten raw.' Poison Toxic Principle: 'Needle-like, calcium oxalate crystals; possible proteins.' Causes Contact Dermatitis: No. Poison Part: Leaves, Roots. Tags include #poisonous. RHS's Potentially harmful field reads 'Harmful if eaten; skin/eye irritant. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling' and 'Pets: Harmful if eaten; skin/eye irritant', which disagrees with NC State's 'Causes Contact Dermatitis: No'. Neither page carries allergy text.

landed.summary: I re-read the NC State and RHS pages with qc.py. MOBOT returned ConnectError and could not be read, as the researcher said, and no field depends on it. All six values hold up. Height and spread are RHS's 'Max Height/Max Spread 1-1.5 metres' correctly converted at 39.37 in/m to 39.4-59.1 in. They are not unconverted feet, and each range matches the page's published band. The page is for the species, the plant is not a climber (NC State: Erect), and 59.1 in is under the 120 in houseplant limit, with RHS describing container growing. is_edible=true rests on a verbatim NC State quote, and the conditions (cooked only, toxic raw, calcium oxalate) plus the full Poison Symptoms text are in unknowns. attracts_pollinators=true rests on a verbatim 'to attract pollinators' sentence and the structured 'Attracts: Pollinators' field. Every citation is labelled with its field name, and every quote is one verbatim rendered run with no U+23CE. Nothing refuted and no quotes need correcting.
